{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 215,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "All-clients permissions are ignored when a client-specific resource already exists",
      "body": "In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), the type-level 'Clients' resource is only evaluated when no client-specific resource is found. If any authorization resource already exists for the client (for example because another permission referenced that client), the method evaluates only that specific resource and never checks type-level permissions. As a result, a grant on all clients for MANAGE, CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, or MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE can be denied for clients that have an unrelated specific resource. The implementation should evaluate both the specific client resource and the type resource, or otherwise include type-level grants."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 219,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "NullPointerException possible when fallback type resource is missing",
      "body": "In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) can return null if the admin schema is not supported for the resource server or the 'Clients' type resource does not exist. The following call authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) dereferences resource without a null check. This can turn a missing initialization or migration condition into a NullPointerException and HTTP 500 instead of safely returning false."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java",
      "line": 104,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Entity-specific resources are created without setting their resource type",
      "body": "getOrCreateResource creates concrete user/client resources with resourceStore.create(...) and updates their scopes, but it never calls resource.setType(resourceType) even though the resource type is available. ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission later searches with resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). If the created specific resources do not have their type persisted, type-based lookups will not find them, so clients granted permissions through client-specific resources can be invisible to getClientsWithPermission and other type-based queries."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 140,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "getClientsWithPermission can return the literal type resource name instead of client IDs",
      "body": "getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() to the granted set for every resource with permission. For the all-clients resource, the name is 'Clients' (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), not a client identifier. The method contract is to return client IDs that have the given permission. Returning the literal type name, and not expanding an all-clients grant into actual client identifiers, can cause callers that filter client lists by the returned set to behave incorrectly."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java",
      "line": 310,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "getResourceName does not handle the new Clients resource type",
      "body": "getResourceName special-cases only the Users resource type. For the newly added Clients resource type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Client-specific resources are created using the internal client ID as the resource name and without a display name, and the all-clients type resource also has no meaningful display name. Consequently permission representations for clients may expose null or internal IDs instead of a client identifier or an 'All clients' label."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java",
      "line": 77,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Provider event cleanup may call unsupported V2 methods",
      "body": "registerListener guards role/client/group removal cleanup with Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, but AdminPermissions.management returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. If V1 and V2 fine-grained authz features can be enabled together, or if V2 depends on V1, removal events will invoke these unsupported methods and may fail the removal operation. The listener should skip V2 or the V2 implementations should no-op."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java",
      "line": 226,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Existing admin-permissions realms are not migrated to include the new Clients scopes/resource",
      "body": "init returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. Realms that already have the admin permissions client will not get the new 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope', 'map-roles-composite' scopes or the 'Clients' type resource. Subsequent creation or evaluation of client permissions in those realms can fail with missing scope/resource errors. An idempotent re-initialization or migration step is needed when the schema changes."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java",
      "line": 214,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Missing null/type validation in getScope can cause NullPointerException",
      "body": "getScope calls SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType is non-null or present in the schema. If this method is reached with an invalid or missing resource type while the admin permissions schema is active, it throws NullPointerException instead of a controlled ModelValidationException."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java",
      "line": 126,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No test covers coexistence of all-clients and client-specific permissions",
      "body": "The new tests verify either a client-specific permission or an all-clients permission, but not the case where an all-clients permission exists while a client-specific authorization resource also exists. That scenario is needed to catch the issue where hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates only the specific resource and ignores the type-level grant. A test should grant an all-clients scope and another specific permission/resource for the same client, then assert the all-clients scope still allows access."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: All-clients permissions are ignored when a client-specific resource already exists
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), the type-level 'Clients' resource is only evaluated when no client-specific resource is found. If any authorization resource already exists for the client (for example because another permission referenced that client), the method evaluates only that specific resource and never checks type-level permissions. As a result, a grant on all clients for MANAGE, CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, or MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE can be denied for clients that have an unrelated specific resource. The implementation should evaluate both the specific client resource and the type resource, or otherwise include type-level grants.

findings.title: NullPointerException possible when fallback type resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) can return null if the admin schema is not supported for the resource server or the 'Clients' type resource does not exist. The following call authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) dereferences resource without a null check. This can turn a missing initialization or migration condition into a NullPointerException and HTTP 500 instead of safely returning false.

findings.title: Entity-specific resources are created without setting their resource type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates concrete user/client resources with resourceStore.create(...) and updates their scopes, but it never calls resource.setType(resourceType) even though the resource type is available. ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission later searches with resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). If the created specific resources do not have their type persisted, type-based lookups will not find them, so clients granted permissions through client-specific resources can be invisible to getClientsWithPermission and other type-based queries.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission can return the literal type resource name instead of client IDs
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() to the granted set for every resource with permission. For the all-clients resource, the name is 'Clients' (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), not a client identifier. The method contract is to return client IDs that have the given permission. Returning the literal type name, and not expanding an all-clients grant into actual client identifiers, can cause callers that filter client lists by the returned set to behave incorrectly.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the new Clients resource type
findings.body: getResourceName special-cases only the Users resource type. For the newly added Clients resource type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Client-specific resources are created using the internal client ID as the resource name and without a display name, and the all-clients type resource also has no meaningful display name. Consequently permission representations for clients may expose null or internal IDs instead of a client identifier or an 'All clients' label.

findings.title: Provider event cleanup may call unsupported V2 methods
findings.body: registerListener guards role/client/group removal cleanup with Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, but AdminPermissions.management returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. If V1 and V2 fine-grained authz features can be enabled together, or if V2 depends on V1, removal events will invoke these unsupported methods and may fail the removal operation. The listener should skip V2 or the V2 implementations should no-op.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions realms are not migrated to include the new Clients scopes/resource
findings.body: init returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. Realms that already have the admin permissions client will not get the new 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope', 'map-roles-composite' scopes or the 'Clients' type resource. Subsequent creation or evaluation of client permissions in those realms can fail with missing scope/resource errors. An idempotent re-initialization or migration step is needed when the schema changes.

findings.title: Missing null/type validation in getScope can cause NullPointerException
findings.body: getScope calls SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType is non-null or present in the schema. If this method is reached with an invalid or missing resource type while the admin permissions schema is active, it throws NullPointerException instead of a controlled ModelValidationException.

findings.title: No test covers coexistence of all-clients and client-specific permissions
findings.body: The new tests verify either a client-specific permission or an all-clients permission, but not the case where an all-clients permission exists while a client-specific authorization resource also exists. That scenario is needed to catch the issue where hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates only the specific resource and ignores the type-level grant. A test should grant an all-clients scope and another specific permission/resource for the same client, then assert the all-clients scope still allows access.
